items.title: Giorgia Meloni Enters the History Books, Pursued by Italy’s Far Right
items.author: Donato Paolo Mancini
items.content: Meloni’s administration on Friday becomes the longest serving government in Italy since the republic was founded after World War II

items.title: Kai-Fu Lee on the Global AI Race
items.content: <article>Chinese artificial intelligence companies are rapidly closing the gap with their US rivals. But AI pioneer Kai-Fu Lee contends the race between the two is part of a much bigger transformation. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: US Grab of Venezuela Denies China Oil, Billions in Debt Payments
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Venezuela is becoming a major testing ground for Donald Trump’s hemispheric ambitions, emerging as another potential source of rivalry with China.</article>

items.title: Macron’s Gulf Push Straddles Divide Between Riyadh and Abu Dhabi
items.author: Dinesh Nair, Samy Adghirni and Omar El Chmouri
items.content: <article>Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s recent trip to Paris showed glimpses of the depth of the French-Saudi relationship. He was spotted with Emmanuel Macron at the Esports World Cup, which was moved out of Riyadh due to the Iran war, and the two unveiled deals spanning everything from technology and defense to a €6 billion theme park.</article>

items.title: Serb President Faces Biggest Threat to His Rule After Student-Led Protests
items.author: Misha Savic
items.content: Aleksandar Vucic has been facing down student-led protests for almost two years. They’ve gone from irritation to a threat to his rule.

items.title: Malaysia Ex-PM Najib Wins Pause on Bankruptcy Proceedings: Edge
items.author: Ram Anand
items.content: <article>Malaysia’s jailed ex-premier Najib Razak won a court bid to halt bankruptcy proceedings against him over 1.69 billion ringgit ($418 million) in alleged unpaid tax arrears, according to a report by The Edge.</article>

items.title: South Korean Cabinet Revamp Fails to Stem Slide in Lee Support
items.author: Soobin Kim
items.content: <article>South Korean President Lee Jae Myung’s approval rating slid to a fresh record low, a sign that his surprise cabinet reshuffle failed to immediately shore up public sentiment.</article>

items.title: Japan Needs to Stand Firm Against US Pressure, Lawmaker Says
items.author: Alastair Gale and Sakura Murakami
items.content: <article>Japan needs to stand firm against US pressure as its close security ally challenges international norms and laws under President Donald Trump’s “America First” agenda, according to a veteran Japanese lawmaker.</article>

items.title: Greer Says He’s ‘Optimistic’ About Relations With China Before Trump-Xi Summit
items.author: Ryan Chua
items.content: <article>US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer struck a positive tone on relations with China weeks before a summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, despite underlying disagreements between the two nations.</article>

items.title: Argentina’s Milei Revives Bitter Falklands Dispute With UK
items.author: Manuela Tobias and Jonathan Gilbert
items.content: <article>Argentina’s Javier Milei is reviving his country’s bitter clash with the UK over the Falkland Islands, targeting a new oil project in the disputed area in strident terms as the popularity of his presidency sinks.</article>

items.title: South Korea Paving Way to Send Troops to Hormuz, Reports Say
items.author: Soo-Hyang Choi
items.content: <article>South Korea has begun preparations for a possible deployment of a naval support ship and troops to the Strait of Hormuz, local media reports said, as President Donald Trump ramped up pressure on the US ally over its lack of support for the war with Iran.</article>

items.title: Trump Attacks Missouri’s High Court Over Redistricting Decision
items.author: John Harney
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump assailed a decision by the Missouri Supreme Court that cast aside a congressional map engineered by state Republicans, likely allowing Democrats to retain a House seat in November’s midterm elections they would’ve almost certainly otherwise lost.</article>

items.title: JD Vance on Iran: ‘I Wouldn’t Call It a War'
items.content: <article>"Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Jim McGovern (D-MA), the top Democrat on the House Rules Committee, says his conversations with constituents are dominated by concerns around the cost of living, arguing voters want Congress focused on lowering prices ahead of the midterm elections. Vladyslav Vlasiuk, Presidential Commissioner for Sanctions Policy of Ukraine, says Congress should pass a sweeping Russia sanctions bill "now," arguing additional economic pressure is needed to constrain Moscow's ability to fund the war. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Powerful Brazil Judge Faces Reckoning Over Ties to $10 Billion Bank Scandal
items.author: Daniel Carvalho and Martha Beck
items.content: <article>For the past seven years, no member of Brazil’s Supreme Court has exercised its vast powers as forcefully as Alexandre de Moraes.</article>

items.title: Trump Names Adam Telle Acting Army Secretary After Driscoll Exit
items.author: Jen Judson and Derek Wallbank
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump named Adam Telle as acting secretary of the US Army, elevating the current assistant secretary overseeing civil works following the resignation of Army Secretary Dan Driscoll.</article>

items.title: Alger EVP: Still Massive Opportunity for AI
items.content: <article>Ankur Crawford, Executive Vice President and Portfolio Manager at Alger, says political backlash around AI infrastructure could become a future constraint on data center and chip buildout, though it has not yet materially slowed projects. She argues that much of the opposition is driven by misinformation and that the key risk for investors is confusion, which can create volatility. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: FCC Tells Judge Trump Clash With ABC Isn’t About Free Speech
items.author: Erik Larson
items.content: <article>The US Federal Communications Commission asked a judge to toss out ABC’s lawsuit accusing the regulator of waging an unconstitutional “retaliatory campaign” against the network as punishment for programming criticized by the Trump administration.</article>

items.title: Farage’s Bid to Reset Reform UK Fortunes Hit By Undercover Sting
items.author: Alex Wickham
items.content: <article>Reform UK leader Nigel Farage’s hopes of using a keynote speech at his party’s annual convention to arrest a slide in opinion polls were upended after two of his closest allies were covertly filmed discussing avoiding electoral law to secure foreign donations.</article>

items.title: Supreme Court Asked to Allow Mail Ballot Curbs for Midterms
items.author: Zoe Tillman
items.content: <article>The Trump administration asked the US Supreme Court to let the Postal Service enforce new rules for mail-in ballots ahead of the November midterm elections, a move that some states have warned would wreak havoc as they prepare to send ballots to voters in the coming days.</article>

items.title: Taiwan Gets Rare Win Over China in Spat at South Korean Art Show
items.author: Yian Lee
items.content: <article>A South Korean art exhibition will allow Taiwanese participants to use the designation “Taiwan Pavilion,” despite Chinese protests, marking a rare win for the island in its fight for international recognition.</article>
